senses.gloss: f. (כּוּל or כָּלַל) [enclosure,] curtain, curtained bed, canopy.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 36">Gen. R. s. 36</cite>, beg. <he>כדיין שמותחין כ׳ על פניו</he> like a judge before whom they spread the curtain (that he may be undisturbed; <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 5:1">Lev. R. s. 5</cite> <he>את הוילון</he>).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 20:1:3">Y. Sabb. XX, beg. 17ᶜ</cite> (in Chald. dict.) <he>ההן כ׳ דעל וכ׳</he> that curtain before the ark.

<cite ref="Sukkah 10b:6">Succ. 10ᵇ</cite> <he>מותר לישן בכ׳ וכ׳</he> it is permitted to sleep in the Succah in a tester-bed though it has a top cover. Ib. 11ᵃ <he>כִּילַת חתנים</he> a bridal bed (without cover overhead).

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 12">Num. R. s. 12</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Song of Songs 3:9">Cant. III, 9</cite>, v. <cite ref="A02817"><he>אַפִּרְיוֹן</he></cite>) ‘the king … made for himself a bridal litter’, that is the world <he>שהוא עשוי כמין כ׳</he> which is formed like a canopy (v.

<cite ref="Psalms 104:2">Ib.</cite> s. 13; a. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="K00529"><he>כִּילָיוֹת</he></cite>, <cite ref="K00529"><he>כִּילָאוֹת</he></cite> (fr. <cite ref="K00545"><he>כִּילַי</he></cite> or <cite ref="K00532"><he>כִּילָא</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 28">Gen. R. s. 28</cite> (<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 47">Yalk. ib. 47</cite> <cite ref="F00040"><he>וִילָאוֹת</he></cite>, some ed. <he>פלאות</he>, read: <cite ref="K00751"><he>כִּילָ׳</he></cite>).
